answer.rationale: Primary contract ends in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line is at 94% with no buffer, so continuity is binding. Incumbent already refused a price reopen, so a negotiate_terms bet may burn the only decision slot and still lapse supply. Switching on c2 could hit the 18% cut but is unverified for a two-week cutover and would likely raise delivery risk. c1 is the only path that historically kept deliveries and integration intact. Renewing is the least risk-increasing option under the stated constraint; cost-cut remains unmet. Verifying c2 (onboarding speed/scope) and c4 (whether renewal-window leverage still exists despite the refusal) before locking further.
